福爾摩沙小導遊臺南 Tainan・中西區

鄭成功祖廟Koxinga Ancestral Shrine

認識鄭成功的日本母親、平戶海灘上的兒誕石，以及兒子鄭經為父親建的這座家廟。

Meet Koxinga's Japanese mother, the Birth Stone from Hirado, and the family shrine his son built.

熱鬧的忠義路上，有一座安靜的小廟。在這裡，我們認識的鄭成功不是英雄，而是一個兒子。1624 年，田川松在日本平戶的海灘採貝，突然在一塊大石旁臨盆。父親是在日本經商的福建人。大約七歲時，男孩離開母親，到中國投靠父親。戰亂讓家族破碎：父親降清，母親過世。鄭成功立誓，絕不投降。1663 年，兒子鄭經建了這座家廟紀念父親。門前的古井至今還在。1771 年，後代子孫留下表彰三代的匾額。如今，來自日本的兒誕石就在庭院裡。

On busy Zhongyi Road stands a small, quiet shrine. Here we meet Koxinga not as a hero, but as a son. In 1624, Tagawa Matsu was gathering shellfish on a beach in Hirado, Japan, when she suddenly went into labor beside a great rock. His father was a Fujian merchant who traded in Japan. At about seven, the boy left his mother to join his father in China. War tore the family apart. His father surrendered to the Qing, and his mother died. Koxinga swore he would never surrender. In 1663, his son Zheng Jing built this family shrine to honor him. The old well in front is still here. In 1771, a descendant left a plaque honoring three generations. Today, a piece of the Birth Stone from Japan rests in the courtyard.

為什麼值得來

Why it matters & history
  1. 平戶海灘的起點鄭成功的故事，從日本平戶的一片海灘開始。Koxinga's story begins on a beach in Hirado, Japan.
  2. 國仇家恨戰亂讓這個家族一夕破碎，也鑄成鄭成功不降清的決心。War broke the family apart, and Koxinga swore never to surrender.
  3. 一座家廟的故事這是一座家廟，比官方的延平郡王祠更安靜、也更私密。This is a family shrine, quieter and more personal than the grand state shrine.

認識景點

About the place

平戶海灘的起點It began on a beach

商人父親：父親鄭芝龍是福建南安人，經常往來平戶做生意。 武士家的女兒：母親田川松出身平戶的武士家庭。 採貝時臨盆：1624 年，她在千里濱採貝時突然臨盆。 兒誕石：相傳她倚著海邊一塊大石生下兒子，這塊石頭就叫「兒誕石」。

A merchant father: His father, Zheng Zhilong, was a trader from Nan'an, Fujian, active in Japan. A samurai daughter: His mother, Tagawa Matsu, came from a samurai family in Hirado. Labor on the beach: In 1624, she went into labor while gathering shellfish at Senrigahama. The Birth Stone: Legend says she gave birth leaning against a great rock, now called the Birth Stone.

乳名福松：他在平戶的乳名叫福松，約七歲才離開母親，到中國投靠父親。

A boy called Fukumatsu: In Hirado he was called Fukumatsu. At about seven, he left his mother to join his father in China.

國仇家恨Loss and resolve

國姓爺：約 1645 年，隆武帝賜他皇帝的姓（朱），又為他改名「成功」，所以人稱「國姓爺」。 父親降清：1646 年，鄭芝龍投降清朝，後來仍被清廷處死。 失去母親：母親 1645 年才到福建團聚，隔年清軍攻到安海，她在戰亂中過世。 終生不降：經歷雙重的失去，鄭成功立下鐵一般的意志：絕不降清。

Lord of the Royal Surname: Around 1645, the Longwu Emperor gave him the royal family name and the name Chenggong. So people called him Koxinga. His father surrenders: In 1646, Zheng Zhilong surrendered to the Qing. Years later, he was executed. Losing his mother: His mother joined him in Fujian in 1645. The next year, she died when Qing troops reached Anhai. Never surrender: After this double loss, Koxinga would never surrender to the Qing.

來到臺灣：1662 年荷蘭人離開臺灣，同年鄭成功就過世了。 兒子盡孝：1663 年，長子鄭經建了這座廟紀念父親。

On to Taiwan: In 1662, the Dutch left Taiwan. Koxinga died that same year. A son remembers: In 1663, his eldest son, Zheng Jing, built this shrine to honor him.

一座家廟的故事A family shrine through time

後人買回：明鄭結束後族人被遷回大陸；1771 年鄭氏後人買回整修，改稱鄭氏大宗祠。 三圭世錫：四世孫鄭汝成來臺祭祖，留下此匾。「圭」是受封的象徵，三圭指三代受封。 神像與牌位：正殿供奉鄭成功神像，以及祖先與夫人的牌位。 1947 年的神像：正殿神像 1947 年雕成，據說依照日本人留下的油畫塑造。

Bought back: After 1683 the family had to leave. In 1771, Zheng descendants bought it back and restored it. San Gui Shi Xi: A fourth-generation descendant, Zheng Ru-cheng, left this plaque. It honors three generations of noble rank. Statue and tablets: The main hall holds his statue and the spirit tablets of his ancestors and his wife. A statue from 1947: The hall statue was made in 1947, said to follow an old oil painting.

被拓寬的馬路：日治時期拓寬道路，前半部被拆，大門退到現在的位置。 門前古井：是建廟時留下的，是這裡最古老的遺跡。

A road cuts through: In the Japanese era, a wider road took the front part of the shrine. The old well: in front is the oldest part of the shrine.

實景照片

Photos on site

國姓爺母子像 Koxinga and his mother

石雕裡，小小的鄭成功站在媽媽身邊。他的媽媽是日本人。底座上寫著，這座像在 2000 年立起。

In this stone statue, young Koxinga stands beside his mother. His mother was Japanese. The base says it was set up in 2000.

鄭成功立像 Statue of Koxinga

一座銅色的鄭成功立像，站在花崗石底座上，後面是綠色的圓窗。底座上刻著年份 2016。

A bronze-colored statue of Koxinga stands on a granite base, in front of a round green window. The year 2016 is carved on the base.

國姓爺的由來 How he got his name

這幅字下面的小字講了一個故事：年輕的鄭森見到隆武帝。據說他說：「文官不貪財，武官不怕死，江山可保矣。」隆武帝很欣賞他，賜他皇帝的姓，又改名「成功」，所以大家叫他「國姓爺」。

This scroll tells a story. Young Zheng Sen met the Longwu Emperor. It is said he answered, "If officials don't love money, and soldiers aren't afraid to die, the country will be safe." The emperor gave him the royal family name and a new name, Chenggong. So people called him Koxinga, Lord of the Royal Surname.

兒誕石 The Birth Stone

木箱上寫著「鄭成功兒誕石」，來自日本平戶的千里濱，是平戶送的禮物。相傳鄭成功的媽媽就在那片海灘的一塊大石頭旁生下他。

The words on the box say this is Koxinga's Birth Stone, from Senrigahama beach in Hirado, Japan. It was a gift from Hirado. Legend says his mother gave birth beside a big rock on that beach.

正殿 The main hall

正殿上方掛著「三圭世錫」匾，稱頌鄭家三代受封。中間坐著鄭成功的神像，後面是祖先的牌位，兩旁各站一尊護衛神像。

The plaque San Gui Shi Xi hangs above the main hall. It honors three generations of noble rank. Koxinga's statue sits in the middle, with his ancestors' spirit tablets behind him. Two guardian statues stand on the sides.

淨手亭 Hand-washing pavilion

紅色的「淨手亭」掛著草繩，有竹子做的出水口和一盞小燈籠，樣子很像日本神社的洗手處。

This red Hand-Washing Pavilion has straw ropes, a bamboo water spout, and a little lantern. It looks like the hand-washing places at Japanese shrines.
